The native engine fits covariance-structure models from lavaan-style syntax by
maximum likelihood. This guide covers the whole workflow in one place: syntax,
fitting, inference, constraints, model comparison, diagnostics and the route to
the mediation objects. It is experimental. For a first look, read
[the five-minute quickstart](native-quickstart.html).

| | |
|---|---|
| **Entry points** | `fit_sem(syntax, data)`; `fit_mediation(model = syntax, engine = "native")` for one mediator |
| **Class returned** | `SEMFit`, then `MediationData`, `SerialMediationData` or `ParallelMediationData` from `extract_mediation()` |
| **Syntax reference** | `?"medfit-syntax"` |
| **Not covered** | means, groups, categorical outcomes, other estimators; see [the limits](#limits) |

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(medfit)
library(generics)
d <- mediation_demo
```

## 1. Syntax

| Statement | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `y ~ x1 + x2` | regression of `y` on `x1` and `x2` |
| `f =~ y1 + y2 + y3` | latent variable `f` measured by indicators |
| `y1 ~~ y2` | covariance; `y1 ~~ y1` is a variance |
| `y ~ a*x` | label a path; equal labels are one parameter |
| `y ~ 0.5*x` | fix a path |
| `start(0.3)*`, `lower(0)*`, `upper(1)*` | starting value, lower and upper bound |
| `ab := a*b` | defined parameter with a delta-method standard error |
| `a == b`, `cp == a*b`, `a*b > 0.1` | equality or inequality constraint on labels, linear or not |
| `y1, y2 ~ x` | comma shorthand (a medfit extension; lavaan reads it differently) |

Exogenous variables get free variances and covariances, as lavaan does with
`fixed.x = FALSE`; `fixed_x = TRUE` in `fit_sem()` fixes them at the sample moments
instead (fewer parameters, the same structural estimates, a conditional log likelihood).
Both sides of a constraint and the right side of a definition
are arithmetic expressions in the labels (`+ - * / ^`, parentheses, `exp`, `log`,
`sqrt`, `abs`, `min`, `max`, `pnorm`, `qnorm`, and a few more).

## 2. Fit and read

```{r}
#| label: fit
syntax <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + covariate1
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment + covariate1
  ab := a * b
  total := cp + a * b
"
fit <- fit_sem(syntax, d)
summary(fit)
```

| To get | Use |
|---|---|
| free-parameter estimates | `coef(fit)`; names are the label, else `lhs op rhs` without spaces (`M~X`, `eta=~m2`), as `lavaan::coef()` |
| the covariance matrix | `vcov(fit)` |
| a table with intervals | `tidy(fit, conf_int = TRUE)`; `confint(fit)` for the matrix |
| defined parameters | `fit@defined`, or the `:=` rows of `tidy()` and `confint()` |
| chi-square, df, logLik, AIC, BIC | `glance(fit)`; `logLik(fit)`, `nobs(fit)` |

```{r}
#| label: tidy
tidy(fit, conf_int = TRUE)[, c("term", "estimate", "std_error", "conf_low", "conf_high")]
glance(fit)
```

The chi-square is $n$ times the minimized discrepancy and has `df` degrees of
freedom. A saturated model (here `df = 0`) fits perfectly by construction, so the
test only means something when there are restrictions.

## 3. Standard errors and weights

The default information matrix is observed; `information = "expected"` gives
lavaan's default. `se_type = "sandwich"` gives the HC0 robust covariance, and
`weights` takes case weights.

```{r}
#| label: se
w <- seq_len(nrow(d)) %% 3 + 1
robust <- fit_sem(syntax, d, weights = w, se_type = "sandwich")
rbind(model_based = sqrt(diag(vcov(fit)))[1:3], weighted_robust = sqrt(diag(vcov(robust)))[1:3])
```

## 4. Constraints

A constraint is a line of syntax. The engine classifies it and uses the cheapest
exact route:

| Constraint | Example | How it is solved |
|---|---|---|
| linear equality or bound | `a == b`, `a + b == 1`, `a < 0.3` | constant Jacobian rows; every accepted solution passes a gate on all rows |
| nonlinear equality | `cp == a*b` | Jacobian recomputed at every point; every start tried, the best accepted one kept; a Newton polish after acceptance |
| nonlinear inequality | `a*b > 0.1`, `ab > 0` with `ab := a*b` | same, as rows $c(\theta) \le 0$; a warning when the starts disagree |
| product set to zero | `a*b == 0`, `b1*b2*b3 == 0` | exact: one linear fit per factor, smallest discrepancy kept |
| sum of products | `a1*b1 + a2*b2 == 0` | best-effort: the best of the starts; a disagreement warning means a better optimum may exist, so raise `n_starts` |

```{r}
#| label: constraints
tied <- fit_sem(paste0(syntax, "cp == a * b\n"), d)
round(coef(tied)[c("a", "b", "cp")], 4)
tied@diagnostics$active_constraints
```

Labels used in a constraint must be defined in the model, and a constraint with
no free parameter is an error. `CONSTRAINT(a == b)` is the same as the bare
`a == b`.

## 5. Compare models and test the indirect effect

`anova()` is the likelihood-ratio test for nested `SEMFit`s; it refits nothing.
Nesting is checked by parameter-table inclusion, a necessary condition, so
two models that pass but are not nested in substance are your responsibility. `mbco_sem()` tests an indirect
effect that is a product of paths:

```{r}
#| label: compare
anova(tied, fit)
mbco_sem(fit, "a", "b")
```

For a chain `a`, `d`, `b`, give the paths: `mbco_sem(fit, paths = c("a", "d", "b"))`
is the minimum of the single-path tests against a chi-square with one degree of
freedom. The null is a union of hypotheses, so the test is conservative when more
than one path is zero (its size is at most 0.055 at the 5% level in the package's
simulation gate).

## 6. Diagnostics

Read these before trusting a fit; all are in `summary(fit)` and `fit@diagnostics`:

| Field | What it says | If it is wrong |
|---|---|---|
| `Converged` | the optimizer returned and the acceptance gate passed | the fit is not returned; the error names the failure |
| `Optimizer status`, `stationarity` | the solver's code and the Newton decrement at the solution | a large decrement means a stall; try `n_starts` |
| `Active bounds` / `Active constraints` | which bounds or constraints bind | a binding bound means the estimate is on the edge |
| `Improper solution` | a negative variance or non-positive definite covariance | respecify, or bound the variance |
| `Multiplier sign check` | active inequality multipliers have the right sign | a wrong sign means an active bound was not optimal |

```{r}
#| label: bound
b <- fit_sem(paste0(syntax, "outcome ~~ lower(2) * outcome\n"), d)
b@diagnostics$active_bounds
```

When a model with a nonlinear constraint warns that the starts reached different
optima, the constraint has more than one solution (`a*b > 0.1` holds for two
positive or two negative paths). The kept fit is the best, but say so in a report.

## 7. From a fit to mediation objects

```{r}
#| label: extract
x <- extract_mediation(fit, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
                       outcome = "outcome")
class(x)[1]
```

`fit_mediation(model = syntax, engine = "native", treatment =, mediator =)` does
both steps for **one** mediator. For several mediators, fit with `fit_sem()` and call
`extract_mediation(fit, mediator = c("m1", "m2"), outcome = )`: a chain gives a
`SerialMediationData`, mediators side by side a `ParallelMediationData`. A latent
mediator works through the same call.

## Limits {#limits}

- **Observed means only.** Intercepts (`y ~ 1`, `y ~ 1 + x`) are estimated for observed variables;
  a free latent mean or intercept stops with "latent means are planned for a later release".
- **One group**, listwise deletion for missing data, **numeric variables only**.
- **ML only**, plus the HC0 sandwich; no robust chi-square, no fit indices beyond
  the chi-square, AIC and BIC.
- **No four-way decomposition** from the native route.
- For means, groups, categorical outcomes or fit indices use lavaan; the extraction
  route accepts a `lavaan` fit as well. See
  [lavaan and the native engine](lavaan-comparison.html).
